newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Penfold sees lower yr profit, cancels sale.
newsitem.headline: Penfold sees lower yr profit, cancels sale.

text.p: W.C. Penfold Ltd said on Thursday it has decided not to sell its 54.4 percent stake in Penfold Printing Ltd.

The business supplies group also said that due to difficult retail trading conditions, it expected the W.C. Penfold group's profit result for the year to June 30 to be substantially down on the prior year.

W.C. Penfold announced in April it would seek offers for its majority stake in Penfold Printing, saying the company would be better off as part of a group that could provide capital for further growth.
However, it said on Wednesday that in spite of considerable local and foreign interest, no prospective purchaser had met the sale price within the time limits of the tender process.

Retail trading conditions over the past six months had been difficult due to disruption caused by a recent restructuring of the company, a flat market environment and intense competition, the company said.
As a consequence, group profit would be "substantially down" on the prior year.
W.C. Penfold posted an operating profit of A$3.77 million in 1995/96. The net profit of A$8.14 million was boosted by the sale of its corporate contracts business.
The company also said it had surplus cash and would make a capital return to shareholders. The amount would be annouced shortly.
It expected to maintain its existing dividend rate. W.C. Penfold paid an anuual dividend of 10 cents a share last year.
